Review MeetMinutes?

Reviewers mostly praise MeetMinutes for saving time with clear summaries, structured notes, transcripts, and action-item extraction, with several saying it helps them catch up on missed meetings or manage busy client calls. Users also highlight strong language support, especially for Estonian and Indian regional languages, and some mention useful analytics. Review Jamie?

Reviewers describe Jamie as a practical meeting note tool that saves time and lets them stay present instead of typing. The most repeated praise is for accurate transcripts, strong summaries, and clear extraction of decisions, tasks, and action items. Users also highlight simple, intuitive use, support across online and in-person meetings, and reliable multilingual performance, including bilingual conversations. Several say it works better than other note-taking apps they tried, and some especially value that it records without a visible bot joining the call.

With so many solutions out there to choose from, to include those provided natively inside of the video conferencing tools, this has proven to win out time and again. It's easy to judge the difference when I get summaries from Zoom, Fireflies, Grain and possibly a few others in a large meeting. The detail, the actions, the summaries alone make even missing a meeting a real option because you don't even need to watch the meeting recording -- just read the notes and confidently know what was discussed (and what actions you were assigned since you weren't there!!). I love the new meeting notes that happen even when it hasn't joined the call directly. Grain has been a game-changer for my meetings. I’ve tried a bunch of other recorders, and what I really like about Grain is its ability to let me chat with the AI using my meeting transcripts to get quick clarifications. I also appreciate that I can customize what’s displayed while recording meetings, so everything looks more on-brand and professional. And I’m a huge fan of Clips, which lets me take time-stamped notes during the meeting. That way, any action items can be captured on the spot, and if another team member needs more details on how to execute them, they can quickly reference that part of the call to get all the context. Been using it for a year and not looking back!

#### What's great [...] Grain genuinely nails what it set out to do: let you actually listen and engage during meetings instead of furiously typing like you're in a court hearing. The real magic happens with the transcription—it's crisp, accurate, and clips itself beautifully. What really impressed me was the ability to take time-stamped notes and turn them into actual clips within the meeting.

Review MeetGeek?

Reviewers mostly praise MeetGeek for saving time in busy meeting-heavy work: they say transcripts are usually accurate, summaries and meeting minutes are especially strong, and sharing recordings, searching topics, and jumping to exact moments in a call are genuinely useful. Users also highlight easy onboarding and integrations with tools like Google Calendar, HubSpot, Notion, and major meeting platforms. Still, feedback is not spotless: a few users want better speaker and accent recognition, more control over when it joins meetings, and broader integrations, while one reviewer reports missed recordings and unresponsive support.
